speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The MLA was last amended in 2018, in part to introduce a designated credit bureau known as the Moneylenders Credit Bureau (MLCB).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: With this, we made it mandatory for licensed moneylenders to submit borrower information to the MLCB and to obtain a credit report of the loan applicant before granting a loan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: Licensed moneylenders must also update the MLCB whenever borrowers repay their loans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The 2018 amendments have helped to professionalise the moneylending industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: To ensure we keep up with changes in our operating environment, the Registry of Moneylenders continues to engage the industry regularly to obtain feedback and identify areas for improvement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The Bill also contains technical amendments to reduce ambiguity and increase operational efficiency for licensed moneylenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: First, the Bill introduces amendments to improve data sharing and usage policies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: Currently, the MLA restricts the purposes for which data can be shared.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: For example, the Registrar is only able to share data with other public agencies for policy formulation or review and not for other purposes, such as improving operational processes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: Moving forward, the Registrar will be able to share data in accordance with and to the extent permitted by a data sharing direction given to the Registrar under the Public Sector (Governance) Act (PSGA).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The PSGA contains the necessary safeguards to protect information that is shared.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: These safeguards include provisions that prevent unauthorised disclosure or improper use of the information shared and unauthorised re-identification of anonymised information.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The MLA also limits whom licensed moneylenders can share data with.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: For example, other than the MLCB, licensed moneylenders are currently unable to share their borrowers’ credit application and repayment information with other credit bureaux offering credit-related information.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: This has hampered comprehensive credit checks on borrowers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: To illustrate this point, let us consider the situation when a borrower approaches a licensed moneylender for a loan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The latter would want to check on the borrower’s credit worthiness including his credit history.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: To do so, the licensed moneylender’s only recourse now is to purchase credit reports from the MLCB, which do not provide a complete picture of a borrower’s credit history.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The licensed moneylender is also unable to approach other non-designated credit bureaux to purchase credit reports on the borrower, as he is not allowed to disclose the borrower’s ID number.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: These credit bureaux will then be able to provide additional information on the borrower’s credit worthiness and indebtedness, leading to more informed and responsible lending practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: In addition, licensed moneylenders will be able to share borrower information with any prescribed person for purposes related to the welfare and protection of applicants, borrowers and sureties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: Licensed moneylenders will also be allowed to share borrower information with third parties engaged to provide IT support or to recover debts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: This ensures the smooth delivery of business operations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: To safeguard information of loan applicants and borrowers, MinLaw will exercise prudence when prescribing the list of organisations that licensed moneylenders can share borrower information with, by taking into consideration whether the organisation has the necessary data protection and security measures that safeguard borrowers’ information.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The extent of the borrower information that can be shared will be limited to what is necessary.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: For example, in the case of purchasing a credit report from a prescribed credit bureau, the disclosure of the identification number of the loan applicant will be necessary.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The Bill will also enable licensed moneylenders to obtain records from public agencies to verify the accuracy of information submitted by loan applicants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: To ensure the security and integrity of borrower information, clause 17 introduces amendments to enhance security arrangements that licensed moneylenders must undertake to safeguard information in their possession or under their control which they have obtained or received under or for the purposes of the MLA, such as preventing unauthorised access to or use of the information.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: Second, the Bill enhances the MLCB’s functions beyond just producing credit information reports and serving as a repository of data.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: While the MLCB was originally launched to facilitate better tracking and monitoring of unsecured loans issued by licensed moneylenders, data held by the MLCB can be better utilised to benefit both borrowers and licensed moneylenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: For example, the Bill will allow the MLCB to provide credit reports of loan sureties to licensed moneylenders during loan applications.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: To illustrate, consider a case where a loan applicant applies for a loan from a licensed moneylender and where the surety has outstanding loans with other licensed moneylenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: Currently, the MLCB is unable to provide the surety’s credit report for the licensed moneylender to independently verify the surety’s debt obligations with other licensed moneylenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The licensed moneylender would thus be unable to make a complete assessment of the surety’s credit worthiness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: Next, clause 20 introduces a new section 74A in the MLA to allow the MLCB to produce business reports for licensed moneylenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: These business reports will assist licensed moneylenders in the development and improvement of their business strategies or practices, thereby raising industry standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: If a credit report, business report or loan information report is delivered in error, clause 23 gives the Registrar the ability to direct these recipients to dispose of these reports within a specified time frame.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: Third, the Bill facilitates digitalisation in the industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: Licensed moneylenders can instead, for example, use their own app, website or business WhatsApp accounts, thereby increasing business efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: As a safeguard, both the licensed moneylender and the borrower must agree in writing on these new modes of communication.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The last area of the Bill deals with miscellaneous amendments that update and standardise provisions in the MLA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The Bill also makes it an offence for licensed moneylenders to demand payment from borrowers of sums other than the fees permitted or sums exceeding such fees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: To ensure consistency in business practices, the Bill extends the deadlines for licensed moneylenders and the MLCB to notify the Registrar of certain events from seven days to seven business days.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The Bill also imposes record-keeping obligations on licensed moneylenders to start keeping loan application forms and copies of supporting documents from the date the loan application form or supporting document is received.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: Similarly, licensed moneylenders must start keeping the note of contract from the date they issue it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: The amendments proposed in this Bill seek to do the same.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for Minister for Law)
text: In summary, this Bill will allow data to be used in meaningful ways that are aligned with the whole-of-Government standards and will facilitate better business practices by licensed moneylenders.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We need to strengthen our system to boost our protection of licensed moneylenders and ensure that there is an even playing field for them within a healthy business environment and better risk management while holding them up to higher standards.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is also important to protect borrowers and sureties to help them better manage their loan exposures.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While they may have access to licensed moneylending services in a fair and equitable way, their personal data, histories and backgrounds should not be used unfairly against them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry share with the House the regulatory and enforcement frameworks to safeguard their data and to limit the usage of their personal information for only approved purposes?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What are the safeguards that MinLaw has put in place to ensure that the prescribed credit bureaus will keep borrowers' information secure and confidential?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would also like to ask under what circumstances would borrowers' information be shared with other public agencies?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry consider building in a process to ensure that this is made known and explained to them before they agree to be sureties for the loan applicants?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can a surety object to a licensed moneylender retrieving his or her credit report?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Additionally, for cases where applicants have access to a free copy of their credit reports when applying for a credit line, could this be provided to sureties as well?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   Next, I have some concerns about the proposed amendment to permit a licensed moneylender to request from the credit bureau a credit report on a surety without having to obtain the surety's consent.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I am generally supportive of this measure, there may be instances where persons who have agreed to become sureties are not aware that their credit reports can be accessed by licensed moneylenders.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry consider building in a process to ensure that this is made known and explained to them before they agree to be sureties for the loan applicants?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can a surety object to a licensed moneylender retrieving his or her credit report?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Additionally, for cases where applicants have access to a free copy of their credit reports when applying for a credit line, could this be provided to sureties as well?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): Finally, I hope that the Ministry would continue to work with the various stakeholders to build up the professionalism of this sector.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The professional standards can be raised, for example, for the engagement of clients and methods of loan recovery without resorting to threatening or unsavoury practices.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Licensees can benefit from more support from the Ministry for the training of their staff.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Before us today is the Moneylenders (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: First of all, I would like to point out the unique role moneylenders play in our economy.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Outside of not meeting the strict criteria of traditional banks, people often seek moneylenders for faster loan approval rates and for the ease of getting short-term urgent loans.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Also, the presence of licensed moneylenders helps us regulate and reduce the influence of unlicensed moneylenders, who are often predatory in their behavior.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: I believe tightening our laws for the betterment of society is an ongoing commitment and these amendments serve to strengthen the role and work of licensed moneylenders.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: For a small but a very competitive economy like ours, these amendments help to further enhance Singapore's standing as a financial centre.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: There are also some potential challenges which the concerned professionals will have to face.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: I would, first, like to address the impact of this Bill on businesses.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Those business owners engaged in moneylending activities will face both challenges and opportunities.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Borrowers with favourable credit histories may benefit from potentially expedited loan approval processes as moneylenders can assess creditworthiness more efficiently.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: These amendments also enhance transparency and foster an environment where borrowers can expect fair and accountable lending practices.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This may lead to quicker assessments of borrowers' creditworthiness.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: It also contributes to a more regulated and accountable financial ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Also, with the Expanded Borrower Information Disclosure in clause 16, licensees will have the ability to request and disclose borrower information for specific purposes, which might provide moneylenders with more comprehensive insights, potentially allowing for more informed lending decisions.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: However, on the flipside, borrowing could be made harder as the enhanced security measures will require increased resources for compliance with the new regulations.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: As credit reporting takes centre stage, it expands the functions of designated credit bureaus through clause 12, which aims to provide more information for assessing creditworthiness through the collection, use and disclosure of borrower information and data.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: While this could be beneficial, it may also introduce additional steps in the lending process.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Borrowers, especially those seeking loans with sureties, will be directly affected.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: These amendments also introduce new requirements for information submission to designated credit businesses and empower moneylenders to request credit reports on sureties without explicit consent.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: These new requirements could impact the loan application and approval process.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: For example, specifically for small and medium enterprises already grappling with higher operational and labour costs, these new requirements introduced by the Bill may perhaps be a significant hurdle.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This Bill also introduces clauses on digital statements and record-keeping.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: While these options could enhance convenience, there might be challenges for borrowers if there is an eventual full transition to digital methods and could deter less tech-savvy borrowers.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The designated credit bureaus will see expanded functions, including the collection, use and disclosure of borrower information.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Balancing the greater need for information sharing with protecting borrower privacy becomes a delicate challenge.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Along these lines, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I have the following clarifications for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Empowering the Registrar to share borrower or loan information with public sector agencies raises questions about the safeguards in place to protect individuals' privacy.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Senior Parliamentary Secretary please clarify on the criteria for information sharing, data security measures and oversight mechanisms, especially in light of recent information leaks?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The amendments also empower moneylenders to request credit reports on sureties without explicit consent.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: I would also request clarification on the conditions and limitations surrounding this provision.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Senior Parliamentary Secretary please explain what constitutes a "wrongful demand" and the factors considered when determining this?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: In summary, I believe the Moneylenders Bill and the amendments protect consumers and maintain financial stability.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Notwithstanding my request for some clarifications, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Members also made comments and suggestions on: (a) usage and protection of borrowers' confidential data; (b) obtaining credit reports in respect of sureties; (c) the offence of a wrongful demand of payment; and (d) Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) measures for the licensed moneylending sector.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: First, I deal with the usage and protection of borrowers' confidential data.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Neil Parekh asked about the circumstances under which borrowers' information would be shared with other public agencies and the safeguards in place to protect such information.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Whilst I mentioned the circumstances and safeguards in my opening speech, I would like to highlight that the proposed amendments are aligned with what is practised across the Government as set out in the Public Sector (Governance) Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Public Service has in place a data-sharing framework and is governed by Instruction Manuals, which amongst other things, oblige public agencies to safeguard data against security threat, protect personal data and access information only on a need-to-know basis.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These data sharing provisions will enable better policy analysis, planning and formulation and better delivery of services.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Louis Ng asked about the safeguards to ensure that the prescribed credit bureaus and other third parties will keep borrowers' information secure and confidential.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The prescribed credit bureaus and other third parties are subject to the obligations under the Personal Data Protection Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For example, they must protect the data in their possession by making reasonable security arrangements to prevent unauthorised access, use or disclosure.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Their ability to do so is something we will consider carefully when deciding whether to prescribe particular credit bureaus to be able to receive borrower information.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On a related matter, Mr Louis Ng referred to the proposed amendments for licensees to disclose information to any prescribed person for purposes related to the welfare and protection of applicants, and sought clarification on what these purposes are and who the prescribed persons are intended to be.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The disclosure of loan information to such SSAs is essential for effective negotiation and should ultimately benefit the borrower.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: More broadly, in deciding whether any person, organisation or otherwise should be permitted access to the confidential information, MinLaw will, among other matters, assess and consider the need for the possible disclosure and consequential benefits.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Next, I turn to the obtaining of credit reports on sureties.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Neil Parekh sought clarification regarding situations where a licensee is recommended to obtain a credit report on a surety.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked how MinLaw will detect and ensure that licensees do not request credit reports for purposes other than to assess the creditworthiness of a surety.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Licensed moneylenders can only obtain a credit report of a loan applicant or a surety when a loan application is received.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is a risk management call and a business decision for a licensee whether it requires a surety's credit report for its creditworthiness assessment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Registry of Moneylenders conducts regular inspections and investigates breaches of the Moneylenders Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This will help ensure that credit reports are only obtained for proper purposes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Members of the public can also lodge a report on potential infringements with the Registry of Moneylenders.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Additionally, Mr Louis Ng and Ms Joan Pereira asked about the notice provided to a surety that his or her information will be submitted for the purpose of obtaining the credit report.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Pereira also asked whether a surety may object to a licensed moneylender retrieving his or her credit report.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As I mentioned earlier, the credit report can only be obtained when a loan application is made.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In other words, the applicant and surety would be fully aware that the licensed moneylender would conduct due diligence to assess the creditworthiness of both the applicant and the surety.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In the event a surety objects to the retrieval of his or her credit report, the licensed moneylender may make an alternate lending decision to manage its risk accordingly.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Next, in terms of a new offence being introduced, Mr Parekh sought clarification on what constitutes a licensee making "wrongful demand of payment" from a borrower.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This amendment clarifies that it is an offence if a licensed moneylender, without reasonable excuse, demands payment from a borrower of a sum that is either not permitted or which exceeds the permitted amounts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The AML/CFT measures for licensed moneylenders are mainly set out in the Moneylenders (Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism) Rules.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These rules are aligned with the international standards set by the Financial Action Task Force.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In the conduct of its business, a licensed moneylender must have measures in place to assess the risk of, detect and prevent money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Measures include the screening of persons and the conduct of customer due diligence.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 5.00 pm.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.33 pm until 5.00 pm.
